messages:
nate (Acme Product): Hey team — since the v6.0 rollout our product's auto-action feature is failing. Tool calls return schema errors or the wrong tool is picked. Immediate customer impact.

ana (Support): Sorry to hear that, Nate. Can you paste a failing request/response + model id?

nate (Acme Product): Here's a minimal repro (redacted):
```
POST /v1/exec HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-v6.0",
  "input": "Summarize and call: lookup_contact(email=\"jdoe@example.com\")",
  "tools": ["lookup_contact" ]
}
```
Response: 422 Unprocessable Entity
```
{
  "error": "tool_schema_validation_failed",
  "details": "arg 'email' missing or null"
}
```
But our payload includes email — sometimes the call arrives with an empty args object or tool resolver chooses `search_contact` instead.

ana (Support): Noted. Does this reproduce consistently for you or intermittent? Also, which region/route?

nate (Acme Product): Consistent on ~60% of requests from us, region us-west2, route /exec-prod. Started right after canary promoted to traffic at 02:12 UTC.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout v6.0 -> v6.0 promoted from canary to 50% at 2026-02-18T02:12:07Z :rocket:

jason (Eng Runtime): Thanks. Please grab two example traces (one that picks correct tool, one that fails) and paste trace ids. Also include request headers and model variant id if present. Suspecting tool-resolver embedding mismatch after tokenization change in v6.0.

nate (Acme Product): Trace ids: trace-20260218-1001 (bad), trace-20260218-1078 (good). Attaching short logs: bad trace shows tool_resolver -> selected_tool: search_contact, selected_args: {} ; good trace selects lookup_contact with args {email:\"jdoe@example.com\"}.

maria (SRE): We're seeing a small spike in 5xx/422 errors for exec-prod in us-west2 starting 02:12 UTC. Latency p50 unchanged, but p95 spiked ~200ms and error rate +2.1%. Billing token counts are steady. Posting quick grafana link: https://graf.redwood/internal/d/exec-prod?from=2026-02-18T02:00

ana (Support): Jason — any quick mitigation we can give the customer? They're asking about rollback.

jason (Eng Runtime): Two short options: 1) Roll back model to v5.9 in routing (fast, will revert new behavior), 2) Disable strict tool-arg schema enforcement per-route (temporary hack) so malformed arg coercion is tolerated. Prefer rollback unless we confirm v6.0 offers needed fixes.

jason (Eng Runtime): Also adding: suspected root cause is an updated tokenization/normalization in v6.0 that changes the model's tool name alignment. The resolver uses internal signal from LM output to map to tool ids; if token offsets shift, model may emit different tokens that map to wrong tool.

maria (SRE): From infra side, rollback is low-risk for this cluster — can execute a quick routing change to pin exec-prod to v5.9 and monitor. If ops agrees, we can target rollback within 10 minutes.

deploy-bot: Rollout command received: rollback v6.0 -> v5.9 for route exec-prod. Started at 2026-02-18T02:29:05Z

ana (Support): Nate — we're about to roll back exec-prod traffic to v5.9. ETA ~10 min. Will update when verified. Apologies for the disruption.

nate (Acme Product): Thanks. Please confirm after rollback if the failing traces now resolve. Our SLA calls for incident mitigation asap.

jason (Eng Runtime): Quick note for triage: please capture a small sample of LM raw tokens (redact PII) and the model's text output that triggers tool choice. That will help reproduce locally. Also include the tool-resolver logits if available.

maria (SRE): Rollback completed at 2026-02-18T02:35:12Z. Metrics: error rate back to baseline within 2 mins. p95 latency normalized.

nate (Acme Product): Verified on our side — tool calls behave normally again. Thanks team.

jason (Eng Runtime): Filing follow-up ticket: BUG-1258 model-v6.0-tool-resolver-mismatch. Action items: reproduce locally, gather token offsets + resolver signals, add a canary test that validates tool-call alignment for critical tools.

ana (Support): Closing loop with customer and offering a postmortem + timeline. Nate, we'll send a follow-up with mitigations and an ETA for permanent fix.

nate (Acme Product): Appreciated. Also flagged billing alert for the surge — will follow up if any anomalies.

maria (SRE): Side note: recommend adding an automated smoke test during canary that runs a handful of tool-invocation prompts to detect tool misrouting early.

jason (Eng Runtime): Agreed. I'll add that to the rollout checklist and ensure canary metrics include a per-tool correctness signal.

ana (Support): Thanks everyone :thumbsup: 

(END OF THREAD)
